# Measuring functions: Norms

## Definition and examples

::: {#def-norm}
## Norm

A [norm]{.neuerbegriff} on a linear space $V$ assigns to each $v \in V$ a nonnegative number $\lVert v \rVert$ such that

1. $\lVert v \rVert = 0$ if and only if $v = 0$
2. $\lVert \alpha v \rVert = |\alpha| \, \lVert v \rVert$
3. $\lVert v + w \rVert \leq \lVert v \rVert + \lVert w \rVert$ (triangle inequality)
:::

[]{.down10}

With a norm we can measure the distance $\lVert v - w \rVert$ between two functions

[]{.down10}

::: {.columns}
::: {.column}
Example 1: Max norm
$$
  \lVert v \rVert_{\infty} = \max_{0 \leq x \leq l} |v(x)|
$$
:::
::: {.column}
Example 2: $L_2$ norm 
$$
  \lVert v \rVert_{2} = \sqrt{\int_0^l v^2(x) \, dx}
$$
:::
:::

## Norms by scalar products

::: {#def-induced-norm}
## Induced norm

Each scalar product $a$ defines the [induced norm]{.neuerbegriff}

$$
\lVert v \rVert_a = \sqrt{a(v, v)}
$$
:::

Example 1: The $L_2$ norm from the scalar product $(v, w) = \int_0^l v \cdot w \, dx$
$$
\lVert v \rVert_2 = \sqrt{(v, v)} = \sqrt{\int_0^l v^2(x) \, dx}
$$

Example 2: The [energy norm]{.neuerbegriff} of the pile is related to the strain energy
$$
\lVert v \rVert_a = \sqrt{EA \int_0^l (v')^2 \, dx + C \int_0^l v^2 \, dx + S \cdot v(l)^2}
$$
